Synopsis:
 The article covers the ongoing US military campaign of lethal strikes against alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Eastern Pacific and Caribbean, launched under the Trump administration in September 2025. It reports the latest strike killing 2 people, bringing total deaths to 223 across 67 strikes. The campaign's effectiveness, legality, and humanitarian impact are heavily questioned — by the UN, investigative journalists, and legal experts — with evidence of civilian fishermen among the victims, near-zero survivor rescue rates, and little demonstrated impact on US drug supply.
